transcript:
This message comes from Thumbtack.
Avoiding your unfinished home projects
because you're not sure where to start?
Thumbtack knows homes so you don't have to.
Don't know the difference
between matte paint finish and satin,
or what that clunking sound from your dryer is?
With Thumbtack, you don't have to be a home pro,
you just have to hire one.
You can hire top-rated pros,
see price estimates, and read reviews, all on the app.
Download today.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Hurricane Esai E.S. is now a post-tropical cyclone,
but flooding from the storm
is still a threat across parts of the southeast.
Hundreds of thousands of customers in Florida
and Alabama have lost power.
NPR's Debbie Elliott describes riding out
the Category 2 hurricane in the Florida Panhandle.
I'm just north of where it came ashore.
I'm about 30 miles inland, close to Interstate 10
here in the Florida Panhandle.
Rain and wind gusts started picking up
late yesterday afternoon.
Most of the businesses all around here
were long closed by then,
including the Waffle House, I might add,
which is famous for staying open
in all kinds of circumstances.
By nightfall, the pine trees outside my hotel window
were just swaying with the wind gusts,
and they started whacking against the building.
Sheets of rain were pounding the window like a fire hose.
That's NPR's Debbie Elliott reporting.
The storm is now bringing heavy rain to Alabama.
It's expected to move through Tennessee
with its remnants bringing rain and possible flooding
to the mid-Atlantic this weekend.
In the Pacific, Hurricane Simon is now a Category 4 storm
as it makes its way toward the southwest coast of Mexico.
Tropical Storm Rachel is expected to bring heavy rain
and strong winds to northern Mexico and southern California.
President Trump took his midterm campaign push
to central New York last night.
Speaking in Syracuse, he urged voters to turn out,
even though he's not on the ballot.
-When I'm on the ballot, we win everything.
When I'm not on the ballot, 48% of you don't vote.
Please pretend I'm on the frickin' ballot, will you?
-Trump campaigned for Republican gubernatorial candidate
Bruce Blakeman.
He also took aim at Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul,
criticizing her handling of taxes and crime.
The president is scheduled to hold a rally
in Clarksville, Tennessee today.
Stocks on Wall Street rallied this week
as investors shrugged off high energy prices and bond yields.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports all of the major stock indexes
ended the week in positive territory.
-Retail fuel prices eased a little bit this week,
but it still cost a lot to fill up a car or a truck
or a commercial jetliner.
Delta Airline says higher fuel prices
took a bite out of profits during the most recent quarter.
Pepsi is also facing higher costs
and plans to compensate by raising prices
for its soda pop and snack foods.
The rising yield on 10-year treasuries
pushed mortgage rates to their highest level
in nearly three years, averaging 7.4%.
Stock investors don't seem worried, though,
for the week that Al gained 9/10 of a percent,
the S&P 500 index rose more than 1.1%,
and the Nasdaq climbed 2/3 of a percent.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
-This is "NPR News."
China and the European Union have reached a deal
that could cut Chinese exports of hybrid cars to the block
by more than half.
NPR's Jennifer Pack reports the agreement
comes after two days of trade talks with the EU,
like the U.S. rebalancing trade with Beijing.
EU Trade Commissioner Maros Seftevich
says the block's trade deficit with China has been mounting.
European governments have been alarmed at a sharp rise
in Chinese car imports,
even as their own carmakers lay off workers.
Similar concerns have led the U.S. to block Chinese EVs
and impose tariffs on China's imports.
Seftevich says they need to protect European industries
and level the playing field.
China, he says, will also lower tariffs on some $4.5 billion
worth of European exports,
including car parts and olive oil.
The deal requires approval from the leaders
across the 27 nations in the EU.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
Authorities have sealed off central New Delhi
to block planned demonstrations.
Thousands of security personnel have been deployed
and protest leaders have been detained.
Transportation has been restricted,
and mobile internet service has been suspended
in parts of the capital.
The protests target a controversial revision
of voter lists that's removed millions of names.
Opposition groups say the changes favor the ruling party
and are demanding the election chief's resignation.
Election officials deny political bias
and say the review is meant to remove duplicate
and ineligible entries.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.

Hurricane Simon strengthens to Category 4 as it approaches Mexico's southwest coast
Tropical Storm Rachel expected to bring heavy rain and wind to northern Mexico and southern California
Trump campaigns in Syracuse, New York, for Republican Bruce Blakeman and criticizes Governor Kathy Hochul
Trump scheduled to hold rally in Clarksville, Tennessee
Wall Street stocks rally for the week despite high energy prices and rising bond yields
Delta reports profit hit from higher fuel prices; Pepsi plans to raise snack and soda prices
Mortgage rates rise to nearly three-year high averaging 7.4% as 10-year Treasury yields climb
China and European Union reach deal to cut Chinese hybrid car exports to the bloc by over half
